beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: Who decides how you speak to your own child tonight? For Arun, it is a man who shouted at him at eleven this morning, in front of his whole team. Arun said nothing. He carried it home.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: His son runs up with a drawing. "Appa, look." "Not now. Can't you see I'm tired?" The drawing goes down. His wife asks why he is shouting. Nobody eats together.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: He lies awake. One friend has a new house. Another, a promotion. And the man who shouted at him is asleep, kilometres away. So who is running Arun's house tonight?

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: There is an old Tamil answer to that, and it is a bird. Look at what Murugan rides. Look at the bird on his flag. Both were once the enemy he went to war against. He kept them.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The oldest Tamil poem to Murugan already knows the battle.

scene.head: Tirumurugatruppadai · line 46
scene.note: Tamil line, and J. V. Chelliah's English (1946)
scene.gist: The leaf-bladed spear that cut down Sur.
scene.pending: VERSE TEXT TO BE SET FROM THE CHECKED EDITION

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: Surapadman earned his power. Long austerity, and a boon from Shiva. Nothing he had was stolen. What changed was what he did with it. The devas were made servants in their own heavens.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The answer to him came as six sparks, carried to a lake of reeds and raised as one child. In the tradition kept at Thai Poosam, his mother places a spear in his hand: the vel.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The festival remembers the war across six days. Brother after brother falls. At the end one remains. And he does something no one expects. He stops fighting, and hides.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: Surapadman becomes a mango tree standing in the ocean, so large it darkens the water.

scene.head: Tirumurugatruppadai · lines 59 to 61
scene.note: Tamil lines, and J. V. Chelliah's English (1946)
scene.gist: He cut down the mango tree of the asuras.
scene.pending: VERSE TEXT TO BE SET FROM THE CHECKED EDITION

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The vel is thrown, and the tree is split in two.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: And here the Kanda Puranam of Kachiyappa tells what happened next. One half rises as a rooster. The other as a peacock. Murugan takes the rooster for his banner and the peacock to ride.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The enemy is gone. What he was made of is still here, and now it carries the one it fought.

scene.head: Kanda Puranam · Surapadman Vathai Padalam
scene.note: Tamil verse, with our own English
scene.gist: One half a rooster, one half a peacock.
scene.src: OUR RENDERING · verse to be chosen from the padalam

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: That is the text. On the fifteenth of November it was played out again on the shore at Tiruchendur, as it is every year. What follows is our reading of it, and it is only a reading.

scene.plate: Soorasamharam, Tiruchendur, 15 Nov 2026 · reported by DT Next and Deccan Chronicle

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The Saiva Siddhanta teachers read Surapadman as the sense of "I" that will not bend. On that reading he was never only out there. The anger at the door, the scrolling at midnight: we add those ourselves, as his tree, hiding in plain sight.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: And notice how the story ends. The tree is not burned to ash. The force is the same; it has been given a rider. Anger with a rider is the nerve to say a hard thing calmly. Envy with a rider is noticing what you actually want.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: In the morning Arun goes to his son first. "I'm sorry. You did nothing wrong. I was upset about work, and I brought it home. Show me the drawing."

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: Nothing else is fixed. The manager is the same. The loan is the same. But for one morning, the thing that was riding him is carrying him instead.

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: The tradition could have kept only the victory. It kept the enemy too, where everyone can see him. So who is running your house tonight? And what would he be, with a rider?

beats.speaker: NARRATOR
beats.say: A note on how we work. Every verse is shown with its source, in a translation named on screen or in our own rendering, marked as ours. Where we add our own reading, it is marked as our note. The pictures are drawn in code, the voice is synthetic, and nothing here speaks for God.
